en.title: Minimum Replacements to Balance Red and White in Two Rows
en.description:
Replace some ? with R or W; the remaining ? may be left as they are. Every row and every column must have equal numbers of R and W. Find the minimum number of replacements, or output −1 if it is impossible.

This site uses a standard input/output protocol; ranges not given by the source are stated explicitly.
en.input: The first line contains N, followed by two strings of length N over R/W/?. The source gives no numeric range; this site uses 1≤N≤100000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: first fill the two single ? cells, then use one double-? column to balance the row counts, for 4 replacements. Example 2: a fixed same-color column can never be balanced, so −1. Example 3: with all ?, both colors count 0 and are already balanced, so 0 replacements.
hints: A ? on one side only must be filled with the color opposite to the other side, and a fixed same-color column means there is no solution. Leave double-? columns empty for now; after the forced fills, if the top row has d more R than W, fill d double-? columns with W on top and R below, and vice versa.
